extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: A publicly available evaluation suite of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks for which prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater. It is used to study whether chain-of-thought prompting improves performance on difficult multi-step reasoning tasks.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated by filtering tasks from the existing BIG-Bench benchmark using predefined criteria, manually inspecting difficult tasks, selecting 23 tasks for BBH, and sampling evaluation examples from those tasks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data came from the BIG-Bench benchmark: over 200 diverse text-based tasks, from which the authors selected 23 challenging tasks and their evaluation examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-rater baselines were created by a team of raters who manually solved each BIG-Bench task and were scored against golden labels; raters worked on a subsampled evaluation set, had a few hours per day, and could use external resources such as the Internet.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper notes limitations of the human-rater baseline, stating it is not representative of the entire population and should be interpreted with care because task formatting/content changed over time and raters used subsampled sets and external resources.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Some tasks rely on world knowledge, common practices, and presuppositions in Western society, and on English-language humor and Western cultural references, which may bias the dataset toward those cultural contexts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Certain tasks depend on culturally specific world knowledge, and some tasks remain difficult even with chain-of-thought prompting, with models failing to exceed average human-rater performance on them.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is used to evaluate language model capabilities across reasoning, natural language understanding, and world-knowledge tasks, including assessing the effects of chain-of-thought prompting and comparing models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Filtered BIG-Bench tasks using selection criteria; manually excluded extremely difficult tasks; for most BBH tasks, sampled a random subset of 250 evaluation examples; reserved three examples for few-shot prompting.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtered tasks to create a clean evaluation subset by removing tasks with more than three subtasks, fewer than 103 examples, without human-rater baselines, and without multiple-choice or exact-match evaluation metrics.
